memories.content: The user completed a routine dental checkup in April 2024.
When the user heard three checkup questions in succession, they asked for the first question again.
At the next visit, when questions were asked one at a time, the user answered each without omission.
The user called to reschedule an appointment at lunchtime but did not reach anyone.
After returning home, the user kept a photo of the paper instructions received at the clinic.
On a day the user put only the visit address in the calendar, they had to search again for the floor.
On a day the user shared the checkup time with their older sister, the sister called to check in after the user returned home.
The scheduling staff at that clinic expect requests to change appointments to arrive by telephone.
Before adding a follow-up visit to the calendar, confirm the date, time, address, and floor with the user.
The local agent can track completed checkups and scheduled appointments but cannot determine whether a follow-up visit is needed.

analysis.overview: The frames are largely complementary: the reference concentrates on dental visits, while the compared frame spans recurring household, administrative, travel, family, and self-management experiences. Their only direct semantic alignment concerns context-specific ways to structure information and record complete calendar details.

relations.reason: The explicit interactive-question and written-instruction contexts explain why different structuring methods were effective and must be preserved.
relations.summary: Multi-part information was handled more successfully when its presentation matched the task: questions were asked individually, while preparation instructions were converted into a checklist.

relations.reason: Both sides support verifying complete calendar details, but the necessary fields differ explicitly by appointment versus application context.
relations.summary: Calendar entries need context-specific completeness: clinic visits require date, time, address, and floor, while official applications require both submission and expected issuance dates.
